extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys, agents) filing U.S. patent applications before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing the physical, formatting, language, electronic-submission, fee, and filing-date requirements for U.S. patent applications (nonprovisional, provisional, design, continued prosecution, continuation/divisional/CIP) and related submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper submissions — physical paper quality and page layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted on paper or by facsimile transmission, and to become part of USPTO records, must be on sheets of paper the same size, not permanently bound, and: (i) flexible, strong, smooth, non-shiny, durable, and white; (ii) either 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches), with top margin at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch), left side margin at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), right side margin at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch), and bottom margin at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch); (iii) written on only one side in portrait orientation; (iv) plainly and legibly written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink or equivalent; and (v) presented with sufficient clarity and contrast to permit direct reproduction of readily legible copies by photographic, electrostatic, photo-offset, microfilming, digital imaging, and OCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These combined requirements are mandatory for paper/fax submissions that will be part of the permanent file. They cover paper quality, allowed sizes, exact minimum margins, single-sided portrait layout, legibility and permanence of ink/printing, and required reproduction contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheets must have no holes
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers submitted on paper or by facsimile transmission and to become part of the permanent USPTO records should have no holes in the sheets as submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for pre-printed forms and double-column reissue copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical-paper provisions for size/format do not apply to pre-printed information on Office-provided paper forms, or to the copy of the patent submitted on paper in double column format as the specification in a reissue application or request for reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submissions must comply with USPTO electronic filing system requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted electronically to the Office must be formatted and transmitted in compliance with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions are subject to separate technical formatting and transmission rules (see USPTO EFS guidance); paper-format requirements do not substitute for EFS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement and translations for non-English filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed in a language other than English must be accompanied by an English language translation of the application and a translation of any corrections or amendments into English together with a statement that the translation is accurate (with specific differences for nonprovisional vs provisional applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), translation, an accuracy statement, and processing fee (§ 1.17(i)) are required; if not filed, applicant will be notified and given time to avoid abandonment. Provisional applications filed in non-English need not include an English translation at filing (see § 1.78 for claiming benefit later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification formatting — line spacing, font, and single column
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification (including abstract and claims) must have lines that are 1 1/2 or double spaced; text written in a nonscript type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, or Courier, preferably font size 12) with capital letters at least 0.3175 cm (0.125 inch) high but not smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 inch); and only a single column of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred examples given. Minimum character height and allowed font styles are specified; deviations risk requiring a substitute specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page (§ 1.75(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract must commence on a separate page (or first page for reissue/reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page or be submitted as the first page of the patent in a reissue application or reexamination or supplemental examination proceeding (§ 1.72(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering requirements for specification (non-reissue/non-reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than in a reissue application or reexamination or supplemental examination proceeding, pages of the specification including claims and abstract must be numbered consecutively, starting with 1, the numbers being centrally located above or preferably below the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph numbering recommendations and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs of the specification (other than in claims or abstract) may be numbered at filing and should be individually and consecutively numbered using Arabic numerals, unambiguously identifying each paragraph. The number should consist of at least four numerals enclosed in square brackets including leading zeros (e.g., [0001]), appear to the right of the left margin as the first item in each paragraph before the first word, highlighted in bold, with a gap of approximately four spaces following the number. Nontext elements and lists are considered part of the numbered paragraph and should not be independently numbered. Paragraph or section headers are not paragraphs and should not be numbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the recommended format ([0001]) ensures unambiguous paragraph identification and is compatible with USPTO processing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alterations/interlineation and substitute specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Interlineation, erasure, cancellation, or other alteration of the application papers may be made before or after signing the inventor's oath/declaration provided the oath/declaration statements remain applicable. A substitute specification (§ 1.125) may be required if the application papers do not comply with paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alterations are permitted but may trigger a requirement to file a substitute specification to achieve compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc submissions — eligible documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The following documents may be submitted on a read-only optical disc in compliance with paragraph (e): (i) Computer Program Listing Appendix (§ 1.96(c)); (ii) Sequence Listing or Sequence Listing XML (§§ 1.821/1.831 and related); (iii) Large Tables (§ 1.58(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only these categories are authorized to be submitted on read-only optical disc under this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc — technical and physical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A read-only optical disc must be a finalized disc conforming with ISO 9660, on which data is recorded permanently and cannot be changed or erased, and be one of: CD–ROM or CD–R, DVD–R or DVD+R. Each disc must be PC or Mac compatible; OS compatibility: MS–DOS, MS–Windows, MacOS, or Unix/Linux; contents must be ASCII plain text (or XML for Sequence Listing XML) and compressed per applicable sections; XML contents must be in XML format and compressed per § 1.834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compressed, follow the compression rules in the sections cited for type of content (Large Tables, Computer Program Listing, Sequence Listing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc — packaging, transmittal letter, and disc labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must be enclosed in a hard case within an unsealed, padded, and protective mailing envelope, and be accompanied by a transmittal letter including: first-named inventor, title of the invention, attorney docket/file reference, application number and filing date (if known), operating system used to produce the disc, and the files contained including file name, size in bytes, and date of creation. Each disc must have a label permanently affixed with: first-named inventor, title, attorney docket/file reference, application number and filing date (if known), date recorded, and disc order (e.g., '1 of X').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels must be hand-printed or typed and permanently affixed. Transmittal letters must follow paragraph (a) format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc — retention, replacements, and incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Read-only optical discs will not be returned and may not be retained as part of the patent application file. Any amendment to information on a read-only optical disc must be by replacement read-only optical disc in compliance with the cited sections. The specification must contain an incorporation by reference of material on each read-only optical disc in a separate paragraph (§ 1.77(b)(5)), identifying each file name, date of creation, and size in bytes (except international applications in the international stage). The Office may require amendment to include the material incorporated by reference. If a file is unreadable, it will be treated as not having been submitted and notice will be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because discs are not returned and unreadable files are treated as never submitted, follow packaging, labeling, and format rules strictly and include a proper incorporation paragraph in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee determination — read-only optical disc submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For application components submitted in part on a read-only optical disc, the application size fee is determined such that each three kilobytes of content submitted on a read-only optical disc shall be counted as a sheet of paper. Excluded from this determination are any ASCII plain text files or any XML files submitted under paragraph (e) that contain: (i) any Sequence Listing or CRF of a Sequence Listing in compliance with §§ 1.821(c) or (e), or any Sequence Listing XML in compliance with § 1.831(a); or (ii) any Computer Program Listing Appendix in compliance with § 1.96(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating size fees for disc submissions, count 3 KB = 1 sheet except for the specified exclusions (sequence listings and program listings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee determination — USPTO electronic filing system submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications submitted in whole or in part via the USPTO electronic filing system, the paper size equivalent is considered to be 75% of the number of sheets of paper present in the specification and drawings for the application when entered into Office records after being rendered by the USPTO patent electronic filing system. Excluded from this determination are ASCII plain text files or XML files submitted via EFS containing Sequence Listings or Computer Program Listing Appendix as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS-rendered documents are counted at 75% of equivalent paper pages for application size fee purposes, excluding specified file types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversized sequence listing fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission of a Sequence Listing in electronic form or a Sequence Listing XML of 300 MB–800 MB filed in an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 or 371 will be subject to the fee in § 1.21(o)(1). Any submission that exceeds 800 MB will be subject to the fee in § 1.21(o)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large electronic sequence listings trigger specific oversized-submission fees; check § 1.21 for exact fee amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of application number
rubrics_metrics.description: Any papers received in the Patent and Trademark Office which purport to be an application for a patent will be assigned an application number for identification purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date for nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application for patent filed under this section (other than design patent or provisional) is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office. For a design patent (except continued prosecution application under paragraph (d)), the filing date is the date the specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112, including at least one claim, and any required drawings are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date. Continuing applications must meet conditions specified in 35 U.S.C. and § 1.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation, divisional, and continuation-in-part filing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application that names as inventors the same or fewer than all of the inventors named in the prior application may be filed under paragraph (b) or (d). A continuation-in-part application (which may disclose and claim subject matter not disclosed in the prior application) or a continuation or divisional application naming an inventor not named in the prior application must be filed under paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different types of continuing applications have specific filing paragraphs and limitations on inventorship and new matter; continuation-in-part may add new subject matter, but other categories are restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing date and cover sheet requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office. A provisional application must include the cover sheet required by § 1.51(c)(1), which may be an application data sheet (§ 1.76), or a cover letter identifying the application as a provisional application; otherwise, the application will be treated as filed under paragraph (b) (nonprovisional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications lacking the cover sheet are recharacterized unless corrected; provisional applications cannot be amended except to comply with statute/regulations after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and nonprovisional applications and patent-term impact
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent under paragraph (b) may be converted to a provisional application and accorded the original filing date of the application filed under paragraph (b) (with fees), but conversion will not entitle applicant to refund of fees. A provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional and accorded the provisional filing date if conversion is timely and accompanied by required fees and at least one claim, but conversion will not refund fees or apply them to nonprovisional fees. Conversion can affect patent term — conversion of a provisional to a nonprovisional will result in the patent term being measured from at least the filing date of the provisional application for which conversion is requested; applicants are advised to consider claiming the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) rather than converting to avoid adverse patent term impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requires payment of specified fees and possibly amendment to include claims; applicants should consider filing a nonprovisional claiming benefit instead of conversion to avoid patent-term loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution (nonprovisional) application — filing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional (but not a continuation-in-part) of a prior nonprovisional application may be filed as a continued prosecution application for design patents if: (i) the application is for a design patent; (ii) the prior nonprovisional is a design application complete as defined by § 1.51(b) (with conditions on oath/declaration and an application data sheet for filings on/after certain dates); and (iii) the continued prosecution application is filed before payment of issue fee, abandonment of the prior application, or termination of proceedings on the prior application. The filing date of a continued prosecution application is the date a request on separate paper for such application is filed. Such an application must identify the prior application, disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior application, name the same inventors (with some exceptions), include the request and will utilize the file jacket/contents of the prior application, and is a request to expressly abandon the prior application as of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The continued prosecution application carries forward the prior application's file jacket and contents, may be filed by fewer inventors under stated conditions, and cannot introduce new matter. Fees for filing, search, and examination apply as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to meet filing date requirements — notification, petition, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application does not meet filing date requirements, the applicant will be notified (if correspondence address provided) and given time to correct the filing error. Any request for review of such a notification must be by petition with the fee in § 1.17(f); absent a timely petition, the filing date will be the date the filing error is corrected. Failure to correct within the given period or to timely seek action may result in proceedings being considered terminated, the application disposed of, and refund of filing fees less handling fee (§ 1.21(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely correction or petition is essential to preserve filing date and avoid termination; lack of correspondence address shortens available remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion subsequent to filing — missing fees, claims, or oath (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date does not include the basic filing fee, search fee, or examination fee, or does not include at least one claim or the inventor's oath/declaration, and applicant has provided a correspondence address, the applicant will be notified and given a period to file missing items to avoid abandonment. If no correspondence address was provided, the applicant has three months from the filing date to file missing items to avoid abandonment. The inventor's oath/declaration may be postponed until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance under certain conditions relating to an application data sheet and identification of inventors and addresses. Failure to pay excess claims fees or application size fees when due must be remedied prior to the Office-set reply time or claims must be canceled, else abandonment may result. If the basic filing fee is not paid during pendency, the Office may dispose of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different deadlines apply depending on whether a correspondence address was provided. Some time limits (e.g., filing oath by issue fee payment) are not extendable under § 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion subsequent to filing — provisional application requirements and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional application accorded a filing date does not include the required cover sheet (§ 1.51(c)(1)) or the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(d)), and applicant has provided a correspondence address, applicant will be notified and given time to pay the fee and file the cover sheet to avoid abandonment. If no correspondence address, applicant has two months from the filing date to comply. Application size fee must be paid when required or before Office-set reply time to avoid abandonment. Failure to pay the basic filing fee during pendency may result in the Office disposing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications have specific short cure periods; failing to timely cure can lead to abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent treatment — examination placement and informalities (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraphs (b) or (d) will not be placed on the files for examination until all its required parts, complying with the rules, are received, except that the inventor's oath or declaration may be filed when the application is otherwise in condition for allowance pursuant to paragraph (f)(3), and minor informalities may be waived subject to subsequent correction whenever required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness is required for placement on the examination docket, but some minor informalities may be waived and the oath may be deferred under limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent treatment — provisional applications not examined and abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application filed under paragraph (c) will not be placed on the files for examination and will become abandoned no later than twelve months after its filing date pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications are not examined and have a 12-month statutory lifetime; claim benefit must be pursued in a later nonprovisional within that period.
